generic.instructions: Implement the requested change with the smallest clear, maintainable solution. Preserve existing architecture unless the task requires changing it.

frontend.instructions: Treat this as frontend product code. Preserve the existing design system and UX conventions, keep components composable, maintain accessibility, and avoid decorative complexity or unrelated visual redesigns.

backend.instructions: Treat this as backend/application-service work. Keep API contracts explicit, validation strict, persistence boundaries clear, and failure behavior observable. Avoid unnecessary framework abstraction.

fullstack.instructions: Treat this as a cross-stack change. Keep frontend and backend contracts aligned, minimize duplicated domain logic, and verify the complete user-facing path rather than each layer in isolation.

infra.instructions: Treat this as infrastructure/operations work. Prefer reversible, idempotent changes, explicit resource/security boundaries, conservative defaults, and configurations that coexist safely with unrelated workloads.

testing.instructions: Treat this as verification work. Test observable behavior and meaningful failure cases, avoid brittle implementation-detail assertions, and keep tests deterministic and useful in CI.

database.instructions: Treat this as database work. Preserve data, make migrations reversible where practical, consider indexes and locking, and avoid unsafe destructive operations without explicit task requirements.

android.instructions: Treat this as Android application work. Follow the repository's existing XML/Compose choice instead of forcing migration, preserve lifecycle correctness, and prefer official Android patterns over custom framework layers.

docs.instructions: Treat this as documentation work. Keep claims aligned with the current implementation, prefer concise operational examples, and do not describe planned behavior as already shipped.
